title: SDK invocation contract adapters: runtime coercers, retry budgets, and streaming ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Provide a small, cross-language library of invocation helpers that make function/tool calling ergonomic and safe across Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go). Focus areas: runtime schema coercion (soft/strict modes), per-request retry budgeting and idempotency, streaming-friendly call wrappers (sync/async iterators, server-sent events), and clear examples showing recommended patterns. The adapter should not require users to rewrite existing call sites; prefer opt-in surface (flags, helper wrapper) with gradual rollout. Deliverables: (1) runtime schema coercer module in each SDK with the same public API contract, (2) a lightweight invocation wrapper that handles validation failures, deterministic idempotency key generation, and retries within a configurable budget, (3) streaming helpers to convert model streamed tokens into typed outputs or event frames and resume safely after transient errors, (4) cross-SDK examples (quickstarts) and end-to-end tests covering interop with runtime fallbacks and model-variant routing.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-language public API documented: python, ts, go helpers share the same function names and options
Runtime coercer supports: strict validation (reject), soft coercion (attempt cast/coerce), and sanitization hooks for unknown fields
Per-request retry budget enforced: max_retries, backoff policy, and total extra-latency cap; idempotency key generation deterministic across SDKs
Streaming wrappers expose an ergonomic iterator interface and can resume with an intermediate checkpoint when backend returns transient 5xx or capacity errors
Unit + integration tests added to each SDK repository; CI gates on contract tests against a local mock runtime
Examples added to docs site and interactive quickstart with Python/TS/Go snippets
Feature gated rollout plan defined and telemetry for validation failures, retry counts, and resumed streams instrumented
tasks: Draft API spec for runtime coercer and invocation wrapper (options, error classes, telemetry labels)
Implement Python runtime coercer and wrapper in redwood-sdk-python
Implement TypeScript runtime coercer and wrapper in redwood-js-sdk
Implement Go runtime coercer and wrapper in redwood-go-sdk
Add integration contract tests that run identical test vectors across SDKs against runtime mock
Add examples: quickstart notebooks, github samples, and docs pages
Add feature flag and rollout script for enabling default soft-coercion for new customers
notes: This ticket arose from several customer support threads where users reported inconsistent behavior between SDKs when invoking typed functions: Python accepted integer-like strings, TS rejected, Go panicked. We must standardize: prefer a predictable coercion policy that can be toggled by customers. Also coordinate with runtime team to make sure error codes for transient stream failures include resume tokens where available.
risks: Different language type systems make perfect parity impossible; prioritize consistent semantics over exact API shape
Automatic coercion could mask user errors and lead to subtle semantic mismatches; mitigate with clear warnings in soft mode and opt-in default
Streaming resume requires runtime cooperation (resume tokens); if runtime cannot provide tokens, we fallback to idempotent re-run which may be expensive
implementation_notes: Runtime coercer: implement a small declarative schema to type coercion map instead of full JSON Schema; support primitives + arrays + nested maps and per-field sanitizers
Retries: expose a RetryBudget object (max_attempts, per_attempt_backoff_ms, total_latency_cap_ms) that SDKs enforce prior to invoking the network stack

Idempotency: create a stable, canonicalized representation of the invocation (model id, prompt hash, function schema fingerprint, user-provided id) and HMAC it using SDK secret to derive idempotency key; document deterministic algorithm so server can verify
Streaming: for Python return an async generator that yields typed frames; for TS expose AsyncIterable and a helper streamToTypedOutput; for Go provide a channel-based iterator and a Resume() helper
Telemetry: attach validation outcome labels (strict|soft|sanitized), retry_reason labels (transport|throttling|server-5xx), and a boolean resumed_stream label
testing_plan: Unit tests for coercer with 120+ edge-case vectors (nulls, numeric-strings, enum mismatches, nested extra keys)
Property tests for idempotency key stability across SDKs using canonicalized vectors
Integration contract tests where the mock runtime simulates transient stream failure and provides a resume token; assert wrappers resume correctly
Load test for retry budget enforcement to ensure no request exceeds the configured total latency cap under heavy backend slowness
rollout_plan: Stage 1: enable for internal and beta customers; gather telemetry for validation failures and retry counts
Stage 2: enable soft-coercion by default for new SDK installs behind a flag; notify users via changelog
Stage 3: consider making soft-coercion default after one week of good metrics, with opt-out available via client config
